messages:
leo: Hey folks, quick docs inconsistency: api-ref/generate.md response examples show a field named `completion_time_ms` (integer ms) but the streaming examples and the SDK snippets show `completion_time` as an ISO8601 string. This is confusing for users parsing server timings.

sarah: ugh, where did the ISO examples come from? I thought we standardized on ms integers for event timings.

leo: example in the Streaming > events section has: `completion_time: \"2024-11-01T12:34:56.789Z\"` while the sync example shows `completion_time_ms: 169...`.

raj: runtime team: historically we emitted both for different subsystems (legacy sync path emitted ms, new async streamer emitted ISO). We recently changed streamer to ISO for better trace correlation, but we should pick one canonical shape in the public API.

mike: SDKs currently parse both forms in helpers (they try to detect number vs string) but our examples only show one or the other depending on language which is inconsistent. Docs linter also flagged mismatched schema in the generate examples CI.

sarah: proposal: document `completion_time_ms` as the canonical field (integer milliseconds) across all response examples and add a migration note: "Older async stream responses may include `completion_time` (ISO8601). SDKs will parse both until deprecation." That keeps parsing easy and numeric math straightforward. Thoughts?

raj: fine with that if we add a short runtime plan to start emitting `completion_time_ms` consistently from the streamer in the next deploy. I'll file INF-1312 to track it. We'll also emit a trace hint mapping ISO -> ms for a short period to ease migration.

mike: OK. I'll open SDK-snippets PRs to normalize examples to `completion_time_ms` and keep a small comment in the snippet showing how SDK helpers normalize ISO string to ms if seen. That way both new and old callers are supported.

sarah: I'll patch the docs PR: update api-ref/generate.md sync and streaming example blocks to use `completion_time_ms`, add a migration note section under Breaking Changes / Migration with an example snippet showing conversion: ```python
if isinstance(resp['completion_time'], str):
    # iso -> ms
    dt = dateutil.parser.isoparse(resp['completion_time'])
    completion_time_ms = int(dt.timestamp() * 1000)
else:
    completion_time_ms = resp['completion_time']
```

leo: docs CI will likely fail if we only change markdown; we should also update the OpenAPI examples. Can someone push an openapi PR?

raj: will submit small openapi PR to change response examples to include `completion_time_ms` and leave a deprecated `completion_time` description for backward-compat. Linking soon.

docs-bot: docs PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/900 (CI: failing - example-schema-check).

mike: sdk-snippets PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-snippets/pull/604 (adds normalized examples + helper comment) - CI: failing because docs generator couldn't find snippet id in docs. Sarah, can you include snippet ids for the updated examples?

sarah: added snippet ids: `gen-sync-response-time` and `gen-stream-response-time` and fixed codeblock language hints. Pushing update.

docs-bot: docs PR re-run: passing. openapi PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/openapi/pull/210 created - CI: passing. sdk-snippets PR re-run: passing.

leo: great. final asks before merge: add a changelog line under docs/CHANGELOG.md: "generate: canonicalized completion time to completion_time_ms (milliseconds); added migration note for legacy ISO completion_time values." Also add INF-1312 reference in the PR description so infra tracks the streamer normalization.

sarah: added changelog entry and linked INF-1312. Merging now. :shipit: 

docs-bot: Merged. All green.

mike: I'll follow up with SDK release notes that recommend relying on `completion_time_ms` and show the helper that normalizes ISO in case users still receive it.

raj: I'll keep INF-1312 on the deploy board and ping infra when ready.

leo: thanks everyone, that should reduce a lot of parsing bugs we were seeing in support tickets. Closing the loop.
